summary: Approved sequence sheets for CVL tablet lot 3 (WA/2020/313): twelve-month ICH stability pulls, HPLC assay and related-substances validation, system suitability and deviation notes. Assay stayed within the agreed limits at every pull and the impurity profile did not trend towards a limit. Corvenlea used this record in its formulation transfer package.

properties.title: CVL pulls and suitability results Rev03

sheets.name: Summary

rows.v: Westravelle Analytical Ltd, a Tarnovell company
CVL tablet lot 3: twelve-month ICH stability with assay validation

rows: Stability of tablet lot 3 under ICH long-term, intermediate and accelerated conditions. Long-term and intermediate pulls at 0, 1, 3, 6, 9 and 12 months; accelerated pulls at 0, 1, 3 and 6 months. Interim review: 31 May 2021.
Assay at time zero was {{PRJ0010:stability.t0_assay}} % label claim. Every pull to 12 months complied with the agreed assay and impurity limits. Full pull data are on the Pulls sheet.
Method validation summary and acceptance criteria
Deviation notes raised during the study

sheets.name: Pulls
rows: Assay as % label claim (HPLC). Impurities as % area. Water by Karl Fischer. Pulls from the ICH chamber programme as recorded on the batch card.

sheets.name: Suitability

rows.v: Method validation summary: assay and related substances

rows: Method validation establishes method performance; it is not sequence-level system suitability. Validation criteria and results are tabulated below.

For each condition/timepoint on Pulls, consult the corresponding WA/2020/313 sequence sheet linked from batch card WST-20-009708. That record carries the sequence identifier, control injections, method-specific control criteria, observed results and acceptance signature. These details are not transcribed here; this validation table must not be used to infer sequence acceptance.

Replacement-column sequence: consult the sequence attachment to DN-02 and the column-change entry in the same batch card. Control criteria and acceptance disposition belong to that sequence record; no replacement-column control result is asserted here.

sheets.name: Deviations
rows: Three-month pull taken one working day late after a chamber door alarm. Sample held at the set point through the alarm window; impact assessed as nil.

Column replacement noted between interim review and nine-month pull. DN-02 and its sequence attachment are the source for replacement-column sequence identifier, controls, criteria and disposition; method validation does not establish repeat suitability.
No further deviations raised at study completion.
